clue.text: Weak sense about black and white's last piece

indicators.note: the word for sense goes around the letter for black, wrapping it

parts.note: to feel is to sense, as with touch
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the final piece of the word white's is its closing letter

explanation.surface: A chess commentator remarks on a feeble sense of judgement about the last black and white piece on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble and weak are plain synonyms for lacking strength or force.

clue.text: Say Arab initially abhors narcissism

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means when introducing an instance
an Omani is an Arab from Oman

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word abhors

explanation.surface: An Arab, for example, is said to abhor vanity and self-love.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissism is excessive self-love, which is the same obsession with oneself as egomania.

clue.text: Look kills

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang a ... hook is a look, shortened to 'a ...'
a slaughterer ... animals, killing them brutally

explanation.surface: A short, menacing phrase as if a glance could be lethal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a butcher's' is British rhyming slang for 'have a look' (butcher's hook = look).
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is Cockney rhyming slang for a glance; the other is the verb for slaughtering savagely.

clue.text: Complex Greek character has mug with beer raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising the run of letters means reading them upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to mug someone is to rob them
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A Greek holds up a mug of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the whole string ETAROBALE upwards, since this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complex is intricate and detailed, which is what an elaborate design or plan is.

clue.text: Bust on returning fresh funds for election?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another means it follows it
returning means the word for fresh is read backwards

parts.note: raw means fresh, as in uncooked or new
a bust is a chest

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about fresh funds being used to mount a bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' reads as a raid or a failure, but it is the anatomical sense; 'on' means after in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund set aside for a campaign, typically a political one before an election.

clue.text: Film director ad-libs the moves around set

parts.note: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane

indicators.note: the letters of 'ad-libs the' are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A film director improvises as he moves around the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a film set, but it is the definition in its sense of fixed or settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Set in the sense of firmly fixed or settled is a synonym for long-standing and secure.

clue.text: Show Spartan having whip-round?

indicators.note: the whip goes round the Spartan word, enclosing it

parts.note: a cat-o'-nine-tails, or cat, is a whip
Spartan means austere or bare

explanation.surface: A Spartan collects money for a show through a whip-round.
explanation.walkthrough: A whip-round is a British informal collection of money among a group; here it splits into whip and round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a type of entertainment staged in a nightclub or restaurant, so it is a kind of show.

clue.text: Being timeless, The Prince somehow reveals code

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters come out in an unspecified new order
being timeless means the letter standing for time is removed

explanation.surface: Machiavelli's The Prince, a timeless work, somehow reveals a secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T (time) from THEPRINCE leaves HEPRINCE, which 'somehow' rearranges; 'reveals' links to the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To code a message is to put it into cipher, which is what encipher means.

clue.text: Sensor locates son in gallery with American friend

indicators.note: the son is placed in the gallery name, inside it

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies
bud is American slang for a pal

explanation.surface: A security sensor tracks a son touring a gallery with his American friend.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE is the Tate, a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste bud is a sensory receptor on the tongue, so it is a sensor for flavour.

clue.text: Charlie on hiking route sees skyline?

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a trail is a path for hikers

explanation.surface: Charlie, out on a hiking trail, admires the skyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skyline' is not the horizon of buildings but literally a line in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrail is the condensation streak left by an aircraft, quite literally a line across the sky.

clue.text: Count on this posh taxi reversing when outside

indicators.note: the word for when sits outside the other letters, around them

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: reversing means the taxi word is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
U means upper class, posh, in British usage

explanation.surface: You can rely on a posh taxi reversing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' looks like 'rely on', but it means do arithmetic on: the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for counting and calculating.

clue.text: Bishop buzzing with energy in gown

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation
a-throb means pulsing or buzzing with activity
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A bishop full of energy sweeps about in his gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose dressing gown worn after bathing.

clue.text: Trinity student stops nonsense

indicators.note: the student letter plugs, or stops, a gap in the nonsense word

parts.note: tripe means nonsense or rubbish
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A Trinity College student puts a stop to nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trinity' suggests the Cambridge college, but it is the definition: a group of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinity is a set of three, and triple means threefold.

clue.text: Sort date out — this to confirm running order?

indicators.note: out means the letters are sorted out into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Fix a date to make sure the running order of a show is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running order' suggests a programme, but it means a vehicle in good running order.
explanation.definitionFit: A road test checks that a vehicle is roadworthy and drives properly, confirming it is in working condition.

clue.text: Such weapons as come shortly to hand?

definitions.text: Such weapons as come shortly to hand?

parts.words: Such weapons as come shortly to hand?
parts.note: weapons that come to hand as limbs, but short ones: little upper limbs, read playfully as the term for pistols and rifles

explanation.surface: A question about which weapons will soon be available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' reads as soon but means of small size, and 'to hand' points to the limbs ending in hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms are firearms carried and fired by hand, such as pistols and rifles.

clue.text: Low born idiot

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An insult about a fool of humble birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low born' reads as one phrase; 'Low' is the definition and 'born' gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bass describes a deep, low pitch in music.

clue.text: Wicked family shows animosity

parts.note: bad means wicked
blood means family lineage, as in 'blood is thicker than water'

explanation.surface: A wicked family displays hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad blood is an idiom for long-standing ill feeling or hostility between people.

clue.text: Notice cut in smart cloth

indicators.note: the shortened notice word goes in the smart word

parts.note: to smart is to sting

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to heed is to notice or pay attention to

explanation.surface: A notice says smart cloth has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' reads as an adjective for the cloth, but it is the verb meaning to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheeting is fabric used for making bed sheets, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Good free network

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: A good free network, as an internet provider might advertise.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of lines, or a network of power cables supplying electricity.

clue.text: Roman's possession in this case?

parts.note: a Roman possessing something has the possessive form, as the apostrophe-s shows, and in Latin grammar that is a named case

explanation.surface: A detective asks what a Roman owned in this investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a legal case or container, but it means grammatical case; 'Roman's' itself shows possession.
explanation.definitionFit: The genitive is the grammatical case expressing possession, as in Latin and in English 's.

clue.text: Operate reciprocally having Virgin Queen inside

indicators.note: the queen goes inside the virgin word

parts.note: intact means untouched, virgin
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Elizabeth I, the Virgin Queen, is said to have worked in partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin Queen' looks like Elizabeth I but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To interact is to act on one another, so to work mutually or reciprocally.

clue.text: Widely shared image includes fibre layer

indicators.note: the image word includes the fibre word inside it

parts.note: a meme is an image passed widely around the internet
bran is cereal fibre

explanation.surface: A viral image features a layer of fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A membrane is a thin layer of tissue or material forming a covering or partition.

clue.text: African leader forced to hold northern city

indicators.note: the forced word holds the northern letter within it

parts.note: made means forced, as in 'made him go'
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An African leader is forced to occupy a northern city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela was South Africa's first black president, a renowned leader on the continent.

clue.text: British comedian Henry provides fish

parts.note: Lenny Henry is a British comedian

explanation.surface: A British comedian serves up some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lenny Henry is a well-known British comedian and co-founder of Comic Relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A blenny is a small spiny-finned fish found in coastal waters.

clue.text: Limited changes involving Liberal — not right now!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the Liberal letter among them
changes says the letters of Limited are reordered

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A Liberal shouts down limited changes as untimely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right now' means at the wrong moment: inopportune.
explanation.definitionFit: Something badly timed is done at an inappropriate moment, not the right one.

clue.text: Celebrity chef's duck pâté ingredient?

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is': the celebrity chef Jamie, of TV fame, is the duck pâté ingredient

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O
liver is the main ingredient of many pâtés

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef's recipe uses duck pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck pâté' looks like one dish, but 'duck' gives O, a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie Oliver is a famous British television cook, a celebrity chef by any measure.

clue.text: Brave husband left to introduce Beethoven symphony

indicators.note: the two short letters introduce the symphony between them, enclosing it

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

explanation.surface: A brave husband leaves to put on a Beethoven symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroical is an older form of heroic, meaning courageous.

clue.text: Party clothes news boss creased

parts.note: a do is a party
gear means clothes
ED is short for editor, a newspaper's boss

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor's party clothes are all crumpled.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog-eared pages have corners folded down, so they are creased and worn.

clue.text: Cover point with erstwhile Prime Minister

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
Edward Heath was UK Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister is fielding at cover point in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover point' is a cricket fielding position, but the phrase splits into the definition and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting case or covering, as for a blade.
